novelty.justification: The claim’s novelty route is primarily a new mechanistic relationship, namely that acquisition is a “causal prerequisite chain” and that “selectively delaying or degrading ... an earlier capability ... causally prevents or slows ... the later capability,” rather than merely a new setting. The closest prior work I found includes “Do Construction Distributions Shape Formal Language Learning in German BabyLMs?” (2025), which manipulates training distributions and measures word-level, syntactic, and semantic learning trajectories, as well as curriculum-learning and developmental-order studies such as “Order matters” and “LMs Learn POS First”; searches used combinations of “language model acquisition order causal prerequisite,” “developmental order syntax semantics training ablation,” “BabyLM construction distribution learning trajectories,” and “causal intervention linguistic capability emergence.” The step from those works to this claim is a natural extension in methodology but requires a new core relationship—prerequisite-specific downstream gating distinguished from generic data disruption—so it is more than a direct transfer or a renamed probing method, though it remains within the established acquisition-trajectory framework and does not constitute a new general measurement paradigm.
